root_cause: Three GET routes in src/http had ZERO touch of any of the 7 T-0662 AUTHORITY_RESOLVERS (or a verified derivative): operational-analytics.ts computed record_sums as a raw full-registry SQL SUM (the exact record-level leak class T-0632 already closed for report-page-render.ts's Floor-1 aggregate — a documented parity gap, ADR-T0726 §5.2) and never checked whether the caller was still an active employee at all; report-page-render.ts's /process-analytics handler consulted no resolver even though its own sibling routes in the SAME file (/render, /export, /data) already had one threaded as a parameter; record-links.ts's own header comment admitted 'no field-level PDP here (no grant resolver threaded to this route)'. A deactivated employee's already-issued access-JWT stays cryptographically valid for its residual ~300s window (offline-JWKS validation, T-0702) — all three routes served full data to such a holder for that window.
resolver_reused: ONE resolver instance (server.ts's `reportAggReadVisibility`, composed once as getGrantsForSubject + loadTenantOrgAncestry -> makeResourceAncestryOracle — byte-identical to records.ts's own resolveReadVisibility wiring) is now passed to THREE consumers: registerOperationalAnalyticsRoutes, registerReportPageRenderRoutes (already had it — only the /process-analytics handler now reads it), and registerRecordLinksRoutes. getGrantsForSubject is a Group-1 T-0662 AUTHORITY_RESOLVER carrying ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL; a deactivated actor's slug->employee subquery matches zero rows -> grants=[] (fail-closed, indistinguishable from an unknown actor, the SAME convention used by every other PDP consumer in this codebase). No second authority path was introduced (NF-1) — no new SQL query resolves an employee slug outside this one resolver's own internals (confirmed by actor-authority-deactivation-gate.sh's FF-0662-2 accounting scan, which found no new employee-lookup site).

policy_per_route.operational_analytics: Entry gate on the WHOLE route (both /operational-analytics and /export): actor must hold >=1 confirmed grant of ANY kind. Grounded in a verified platform invariant, NOT a guess: migrations 117 ('default-open READ grant... role-reader') and 124 ('read_grant_all_staff_backfill... EVERY EXISTING human staff member... NEW hires already get role-reader from [hire flow]') guarantee every ACTIVE human employee holds at least the role-reader grant — so grants=[] reliably signals 'deactivated or unknown', never 'legitimately active but privilege-less'. workload_daily/weekly/monthly + top_actors (choros.audit_event telemetry, not choros.record) are NOT narrowed per-record — this directly reaffirms ADR-T0632's own written precedent for the SAME data class ('process telemetry, NOT choros.record... no change needed', originally written about /process-analytics but audit_event-sourced data structurally identical here) — they are protected by the entry gate only. record_sums (choros.record, the actual T-0632-parity leak) IS narrowed to READ-PDP-visible records via a bounded scan + isRecordReadable, mirroring runVisibilityFilteredMetric's discipline exactly. Denial: 403 NO_READ_GRANT (zero grants) for the whole route; record_sums additionally degrades to an honestly-narrower (possibly empty) aggregate for an actor who passes the entry gate but holds no covering RECORD-scope grant.
policy_per_route.process_analytics: Identical entry gate (>=1 confirmed grant), reusing the resolver already threaded into registerReportPageRenderRoutes — zero new server.ts wiring for this route specifically. cycleTime/actorBreakdown (audit_event telemetry) are NOT touched beyond the entry gate — ADR-T0632 already audited this EXACT route and explicitly declined record-level narrowing ('process telemetry, NOT choros.record... no change needed'); this task closes only the entry-gate gap the judge flagged, does not reopen that decision. Denial: 403 NO_READ_GRANT.
policy_per_route.record_links: The SOURCE record (the record whose card is being viewed) is gated via isRecordReadable — the SAME predicate GET /api/records/:id (records.ts) uses. Denial: the SAME 404 NOT_FOUND as 'record not in tenant' (not a distinct 403) — mirrors records.ts's own honest-404 convention so a caller cannot distinguish 'record doesn't exist' from 'record exists but you can't read it' (no existence leak). The TARGET (hop) record's field-level redaction remains explicitly FUTURE (already documented in the file before this task, unchanged) — out of scope: the judge's finding was 'no grant resolver threaded to this route AT ALL', not 'hop-level redaction missing'; closing the source-record gate is the proportionate, minimal fix for that specific finding.

top_actors_decision: The task explicitly asked whether cross-employee top_actors (operational-analytics) should be narrowed to visible actors or gated behind a privilege. Neither: top_actors (and workload_*) is audit_event telemetry, structurally identical to the process-analytics data ADR-T0632 already classified as NOT a record-scope READ-PDP surface — narrowing 'visible actors' has no well-defined meaning here (there is no per-employee grant surface over audit_event, unlike per-record grants over choros.record). Instead it is protected the SAME way spend.ts ('any tenant member can view spend', ratified in-file) and org.ts's roster (ADR-T0658 §3.4 'display list' doctrine) already are in this codebase for comparably-sensitive tenant-uniform observability data — EXCEPT this task additionally closes the ACTOR_ACTIVE gap those two siblings still have (out of this task's turf, not touched) via the new entry gate. Documented explicitly in docs/tasks/T-0739.adr.md §3.1, not a silent choice.
